release_name: Updates that reload; location that refreshes
notes: Three fixes, one of them found only by testing the first two. (1) forceUpdate is now driven by the controllerchange EVENT rather than by the function still being on the stack. Previously an event arriving after the 6-second deadline set a local flag that nothing read, because the function had already returned - the update completed and the page never reloaded, leaving the banner up. That path became MORE likely after v27.6.7, because install now re-downloads every CORE asset. The 6s point now only shows a slow-update hint; the reload can still happen, with a real 60s give-up that leaves the app able to retry, truthful reporting on a rejected update, and a guard so repeated taps cannot arm a second listener or timer. (2) THE RELOAD ITSELF WAS A NO-OP: location.replace() to a URL identical to the current one does not reload, so even a fully successful update left the user on the old page with the banner still showing - the exact symptom the update was meant to clear. It now reloads when there is no query string to drop and replaces only when there is. This was not on the list of known problems; it surfaced while testing the state machine. (3) Geolocation: the watchdog now retires the request id, so a callback arriving after a reported timeout can no longer drag the user back into Near me from wherever they had moved on to; and a deliberate action - tapping Near me or Retry - re-acquires the position instead of reusing the first fix of the session, which meant someone travelling across the island was still sorted by where they started. No data change: 426 rows.
